column1: Maximum Subarray — given int array `nums`, return the largest sum of any contiguous NON-EMPTY subarray. Example: [-2,1,-3,4,-1,2,1,-5,4] → 6 (subarray [4,-1,2,1]); [5,4,-1,7,8] → 23.
column2: PATTERN: Kadane's algorithm. | INSIGHT: At each i, decide: start fresh at nums[i] or extend the running sum cur+nums[i]. Track best so far. | STEPS: 1) cur=ans=nums[0]. 2) For x in nums[1:]: cur=max(x, cur+x); ans=max(ans, cur). 3) Return ans. | TIME/SPACE: O(n) / O(1). | PITFALL: Subarray must be NON-EMPTY — initialize cur=ans=nums[0], not 0.

column1: Maximum Sum Circular Subarray — same as Maximum Subarray but the array is CIRCULAR (wraps from end to start). Example: [5,-3,5] → 10 (wrap: [5,5]); [3,-1,2,-1] → 4.
column2: PATTERN: Kadane twice + total trick. | INSIGHT: Either the answer is a regular subarray (Kadane on nums) OR it wraps = total - (min subarray). Handle the all-negative case separately. | STEPS: 1) max_sum = Kadane(nums). 2) min_sum = Kadane(-nums) negated (or write a min-Kadane). 3) total=sum(nums). 4) If max_sum<0: return max_sum (all negative — wrap would yield empty subarray). 5) Return max(max_sum, total-min_sum). | TIME/SPACE: O(n) / O(1). | PITFALL: All-negative edge case — without it you'd return 0 from an empty wrap subarray.
